clue.text: Small bird flew all over the place with tits

indicators.note: something all over the place is scattered in disorder, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A little bird flies about wildly among a flock of tits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' shuffles FLEW and TITS together; 'with' simply joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A swiftlet is a small cave-nesting relative of the swift found in Asia and Oceania.

clue.text: Danish city united in organisation of drivers on right-hand side, primarily

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation

indicators.note: in places the letter for united inside the letters that follow

parts.note: RH is the standard abbreviation for right hand

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word side

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A Danish city where a united motoring body puts drivers on the right-hand side first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes just S from 'side'; 'in' puts U inside RHS, giving RHUS after AA. The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aarhus is Denmark's second-largest city, on the east coast of Jutland.

clue.text: People who provide rooms with insulation film (concerned with loss of life)?

definitions.text: People who provide rooms with insulation

explanation.surface: Workers lining rooms and a film about death, set side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in two parts, the first is a jokey literal reading: those who line flats; the second is the 1990 Hollywood film about medical students who stop their hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the word means fitters who line flats (apartments); it is also the title of a 1990 thriller about students inducing near-death experiences.

clue.text: The writer's singular US composer

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and the writer's is read as I have, contracted
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: The writer claims an American composer is one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer's' is read as 'the writer has', the setter speaking of themself: I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was a pioneering American modernist who wrote symphonies and songs while working in insurance.

clue.text: Equipment of war craft carrying graduate soldiers

indicators.note: carrying means the word for craft holds the following pieces inside it

parts.note: a craft is a skill or art
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate degree
soldiers are men, in the military sense of the rank and file

explanation.surface: A warship's hardware, with graduates and soldiers aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a vessel of war but means skill; 'carrying' puts the graduate and soldiers inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Armament is the weaponry and military hardware a force or vessel carries.

clue.text: Complaint of scrubber in duke's home as 'e frolics

indicators.note: frolics suggests romping about, so the preceding letters caper into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here, giving the five letters of dukes
an aitch-dropped he, leaving only the letter e

explanation.surface: A cleaner larks about in a nobleman's house, cockney-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolics' rearranges IN DUKES HOME AS, and the dropped-aitch ''e' supplies the final E. 'Scrubber' is a cleaner, not the insulting slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemaid's knee is bursitis of the kneecap, traditionally caused by kneeling to scrub floors.

clue.text: Usher in animal, extremely limited by its group?

indicators.note: limited by means the outer letters of animal are hemmed in by the group word

parts.note: a herd is the group an animal belongs to

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the extremes of the word animal, its first and last

explanation.surface: An animal is shepherded in, kept in check by the rest of its group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes A and L, the first and last letters of 'animal'; 'limited by' puts them inside HERD.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to announce or introduce its arrival, as a harbinger does.

clue.text: Rendition of Move Closer, whale activists' anthem

indicators.note: a rendition is a version or interpretation, so these letters are rendered in another order

explanation.surface: Campaigners for whales sing their own version of a pop song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rendition of' suggests a cover version but rearranges MOVE CLOSER WHALE.
explanation.definitionFit: This gospel-derived song became the signature protest song of the US civil rights movement.

clue.text: Small fairylike creature, to trick ugly one, outwardly exuded calm

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an elf is a small creature of folklore
to con someone is to trick them
a troll is an ugly creature of folklore

indicators.note: outwardly asks for the outside letters of the word exuded, its first and last

explanation.surface: A little elf plays a trick on an ugly creature yet keeps a calm exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' takes ED, the first and last letters of 'exuded'. 'exuded calm' looks like a phrase, but 'calm' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-controlled keeps their emotions in check, staying composed and restrained.

clue.text: Take part in rejection of Heathcliff

indicators.note: rejection here means being thrown back, so the letters read in the other direction
part in means a run of letters lies inside the name Heathcliff

explanation.surface: Someone plays a role in the spurning of the Wuthering Heights hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in' points to HCLIF inside 'Heathcliff'; 'rejection of' turns it round. 'Take part in' reads as one phrase, but 'Take' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To filch is to pilfer or pinch something, so take in the sense of steal.

clue.text: Time when accommodation by church leads to a divide in Australasia

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
a manse is a minister's house, provided by the church

explanation.surface: A moment when a church house sets the pace for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' just joins the pieces in order: T, AS, MANSE, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasman Sea is the stretch of ocean separating Australia from New Zealand.

clue.text: Paltry clothing picks out sycophant

indicators.note: clothing means the word for paltry is wrapped around the jumbled letters

parts.note: paltry means small or little

indicators.note: out signals the word picks is put out of order

explanation.surface: Shabby clothes single out a toady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the fodder as CKSPI; 'clothing' wraps the word for paltry round it, split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lickspittle is a fawning toady who flatters the powerful, much like a bootlicker.

clue.text: Alaska etc's forced to get some education

indicators.note: forced suggests being pushed out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here, giving four letters

explanation.surface: Alaskans and others are made to go to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges ALASKA plus ETCS; the apostrophe in 'etc's' is ignored but its S is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a class means attending a lesson or course, so learning something.

clue.text: Slander starts to mount up distressingly

indicators.note: starts to asks for the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Defamation begins to pile up in an upsetting way.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud is a figurative term for damaging accusations, as in mudslinging.

clue.text: Dubious, with front section flipped over bald patch

indicators.note: only the front section, the first word of the two-word phrase for dubious, is turned back to front

parts.note: dubious means uncertain or not sure

explanation.surface: Someone is uncertain, with a forelock flicked over a balding spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with front section flipped' reverses only NOT in NOT SURE, giving TON; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown on a monk's head, so a deliberately bare patch.

clue.text: Relieve Polish, overthrown in United Nations meeting-place

indicators.note: in places the turned word for polish inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a den is a haunt or meeting place

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the word for polish is read in the other direction

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it to a shine

explanation.surface: A Polish leader toppled at the United Nations seeks relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb; 'overthrown' turns its synonym round, and 'in' sets that inside the two-piece meeting-place.
explanation.definitionFit: To unburden someone is to lift a load or worry from them, so to ease them.

clue.text: Strip connects more than one pool

parts.note: a strip is a team's kit, the uniform worn in sport
connects means ties, as in links together

explanation.surface: A band joins several swimming pools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' is the British word for a sports team's outfit, its KIT. 'Pool' is the pot of money in a card game, not water.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared fund or pot of stakes in a game, so the plural means several such funds.

clue.text: African people make a case against holding Europeans

indicators.note: holding means the word for taking legal action wraps around the Europeans

parts.note: to sue is to bring a legal case against someone
Danes are Europeans from Denmark

explanation.surface: Africans file a lawsuit against detaining people from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a case against' sounds like arguing, but it is the legal verb; 'holding' wraps it round the Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudanese are the people of Sudan, a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Unusual to make withdrawal without a slip

indicators.note: without means the letter a is dropped from the turned word
withdrawal suggests drawing back, so the word for unusual is read in the other direction

parts.note: unusual means rare

explanation.surface: It is rare to pull out of something without making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make withdrawal' turns RARE into ERAR; 'without a' removes one A, leaving the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake or slip up.

clue.text: Mock test, an unknown quantity after sign of doubt

indicators.note: after places the test and the unknown quantity behind the sign of doubt

parts.note: er is the hesitant sound people make when unsure
the SAT is a standard US college admissions test
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A practice exam, with an unknown element following a moment of hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like a mock exam, matching 'test', but it is the adjective meaning fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation or substitute, so something sham.

clue.text: Doctor's craft, cutting foot, ultimately considered perverted

indicators.note: cutting means the Doctor's vessel slices into the word for foot

parts.note: the foot of something is its base
the TARDIS is the time machine flown by the Doctor in the BBC series Doctor Who

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the word considered

explanation.surface: A medic's skill, amputating a foot, is finally judged warped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor's craft' suggests medicine but is the TARDIS, the time-travelling police box of the British TV series Doctor Who; 'cutting' puts it in BASE, and 'ultimately' adds D.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastardised means corrupted or debased from an original form.

clue.text: Lower the tone of discussion, having succeeded for time

indicators.note: for here means one letter stands in place of another in the word for discussion

parts.note: a debate is a formal discussion
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of rulers

explanation.surface: A debate gets coarser once someone has taken over for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having succeeded for time' means S replaces T in DEBATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase something is to reduce its quality or dignity, to degrade it.

clue.text: Power source for spacecraft's trajectory length once behind sun

indicators.note: behind places the trajectory and the old length after the word for sun

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
an arc is the curved path of a trajectory
an ell is an old measure of length, once used for cloth

explanation.surface: A rocket's path, once long, trails behind the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks ELL as an obsolete unit of length; the 's of 'spacecraft's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar cell is a photovoltaic panel unit that turns sunlight into electricity, widely used on satellites.

clue.text: Book seizure, as taking every other instalment

indicators.note: every other instalment means alternate letters are taken from seizure and as

explanation.surface: Someone has a fit while reading a serial in odd episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'seizure, as' starting from the second: E, Z, R, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, named after the scribe who led Jews back from Babylon.

clue.text: North invades to occupy African land

indicators.note: invades means the abbreviation for north goes into the phrase for occupying

parts.note: to be in a place is to occupy it

explanation.surface: Northern forces move in to occupy an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to occupy' is read as the phrase 'be in', which 'invades' splits after its second letter to admit N.
explanation.definitionFit: Benin is a West African country, formerly Dahomey.

clue.text: Prophetic trio somehow twists her desire

indicators.note: somehow suggests things done in some unexplained way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somehow a woman's longing gets twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges TWISTS HER DESIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the three witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth who foretell his rise to the throne.
